items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Walker and I rode with Bull.

ctx.x: and I could tell that he was trying to play Rex Stewart's style of playing which was very fast. We started talking and he told me that his name was Roy Eldridge. He also told me that he was married and he was only 17. I don't know if it was true, but after I got to know Roy better, I believe that he could have been married because he was wild enough to do many things that most boys his age would not think of doing.

Shortly after we came back to Springfield from Pittsburgh, Bull William lost his father and inherited a model T Ford coupe. When we went on trips to different places Walker and I rode with Bull. The T Ford would run alright on a level road but when we came to a hill, if it was very long the radiator would heat up and steam would be coming from it like a puffing locomotive and we would have to stop and let it cool off. If we were near someone's house when this happened, we would ask for a pail of water and when…

We drove to Pittsburg in this Ford one time and as Pittsburgh was a very hilly town, and when we were going down hill the car would coast down and Bull would give it the gas ans we would make the maximum speed possible to get up the next hill.
